newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police arrest right-winger for Cape blast.
newsitem.headline: S.African police arrest right-winger for Cape blast.

text.p: South African police on Monday arrested one of three white right-wingers wanted in connection with Christmas Eve bombings that killed four people in a small farming town near Cape Town.
Three children and an adult were killed and dozens of people injured when two pipe bombs exploded in a supermarket in Worcester northeast of Cape Town.

"Jan de Wet was arrested this morning (Monday) on a small-holding outside Randfontein (near Johannesburg) in possession of a stolen vehicle and illegal firearms," senior police spokesman Joseph Ngobeni told Reuters.
De Wet had earlier been named as one of three people being sought in connection with the bominbgs.

Police are still searching for another two whites who, like de Wet, had already been convicted of murder in absentia for planting other bombs that killed 20 people on the eve of South Africa's historic all-race election in April 1994.
The men were among four members of the neo-Nazi Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB) who escaped from custody in March last year, weeks before their convictions were handed down.
A total of nine AWB members were sentenced to 26 years in jail each for the election bombs that went off in and around Johannesburg and its international airport.

Ngobeni said the property where de Wet was arrested belonged to a general in the AWB, whose leader Eugene Terre Blanche issued frequent warnings of civil war ahead of the 1994 election, demanding self-rule for Afrikaners.
Terre Blanche has said his group did not carry out the Worcester attacks, but "understood the degree of frustration" of right-wingers.

A telephone caller claiming to represent the previously unknown Boere Attack Troops (BAT) told state television the group was responsible for the Worcester attack as well as three bombings over the past weekend near Johannesburg.
The caller said his group was opposed to Moslems and communists because they rejected Christianity.
The man claimed to recognise Mandela as president and accepted blacks as indigenous South Africans, but wanted, among other things, all Indians thrown out of parliament.
Police arrested two white mineworkers on Sunday after the blasts in and around the conservative platinum mining town of Rustenburg in North West province.
President Nelson Mandela on Monday vowed to use the full might of the government against bombers who launched a "dastardly" campaign of violence.
